deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 18-21 of cote 120): Grothendieck axiomatises a 'tame' (modérée) geometry over a set R. For each n there is a family M_n of 'moderate' subsets of R^n, subject to axioms (M1)...(M10). These give a category Esp_M of moderate spaces with finite projective limits. Moderate maps are maps whose graphs are moderate. R_0 denotes the points x of R with {x} moderate. The moderate sets behave like bounded or compact pieces: the previous page identifies compact parts with parts contained in a moderate part, and (M8) says R is a union of moderate parts, so R and R^I are only ind-moderate.

Section VI drops the topology and assumes instead that R is a field. Beyond (M1) and (M4), which are the minimum needed to build Esp_M with its finite limits, he imposes (M11).
(a) 0 and 1 lie in R_0, i.e. {0} and {1} are in M_1.
(b) For every A in M_2, addition and multiplication restricted to A are moderate: the sets {(x,y,x+y) : (x,y) in A} and {(x,y,xy) : (x,y) in A} are in M_3.
(c) For every moderate A contained in R^*, A^{-1} is contained in some moderate B.
The marginal 'OBS B = A^{-1}!' is correct. Given B, apply (b) to A×B, cut the graph of multiplication by z in {1}, and project. This shows that the graph of inversion on A is moderate, hence A^{-1} itself is moderate as a projection.

A first version, now struck, asked only that negation x -> -x be moderate on moderate sets. It was replaced by the ring-operation axiom, restricted to moderate domains. This restriction is the essential 'bounded/local' feature, since R^2 itself need not be moderate. The marginal NB records that if R^2 is moderate, (b) is simply the statement for A = R^2. That is exactly a definable field structure, as in an o-minimal expansion of a field.

Stated equivalence: (a)+(b) are equivalent to the Proposition. For a moderate space X, the moderate functions X -> R form a subring of the ring of all scalar functions on X. In particular R_0 is a subring of R, and the moderate function rings are R_0-algebras.
Proof of the Proposition: (f,g) : X -> R^2 is moderate with moderate image A. Compose with + or × on A.

The next page continues the thread:
- R_0-polynomial maps R^I -> R are ind-moderate.
- Using (c), a moderate f is invertible in the ring of moderate functions iff it does not vanish. This reduces to inversion being moderate on a moderate A in R^*.
- So R_0 is in fact a subfield, the analogue of dcl(empty set).
errors: Small gap: to get a ring one needs -f, i.e. -1 in R_0 (or a negation axiom, which he struck out). This does not follow from (a)+(b) alone. It does follow if -1 lies in some moderate set C (e.g. by (M8)): take the graph of + on C×{1}, intersect with z=0, and project to get {-1}. With R^2 moderate it is immediate. The claimed equivalence '(a),(b) <=> Proposition' therefore tacitly uses (M8), or that R is moderate, or the struck negation axiom.
The Proposition also uses that images of moderate sets under moderate maps are moderate (closure under projection). Presumably this is among (M1)-(M10), but it is not restated here.

ideas.what: Axiomatic system of 'moderate' subsets of R^n, now compatible with a field structure on R
ideas.modern_name: o-minimal (or definable) expansion of a field; structure in the sense of van den Dries
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984): programme of 'topologie modérée' only, without these explicit axioms

ideas.what: Field operations required to be moderate only on moderate (bounded-type) domains, with R itself merely ind-moderate
ideas.modern_name: bounded or locally definable variants: ind-definable sets, locally o-minimal structures, o-minimal structures on bounded sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Delfs-Knebusch (locally semialgebraic spaces, 1985); Shiota (X-sets, 1997); Toffalori-Vozoris (locally o-minimal, 2000s)

ideas.what: Moderate functions on a moderate space form a ring (an R_0-algebra); invertible iff nowhere vanishing; constants R_0 form a subfield
ideas.modern_name: ring of definable functions; definable closure of the empty set dcl(∅) is a subfield
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in model theory / o-minimality (van den Dries, Tame topology and o-minimal structures, 1998)

missed.claim: This is an explicit, pre-o-minimality axiomatisation of tame structures over a field. Its notable feature is that it is local or bounded: the ring operations are required to be moderate only on moderate subsets of R^2, R is only ind-moderate, and the equivalence with 'moderate functions form an R_0-algebra' is made explicit. It documents that Grothendieck's tame-topology programme concretely reached definable expansions of fields with a bounded/ind formalism, not just the vague programme of the Esquisse.
missed.quote: ∀ A ∈ M_2, les fonctions (x,y)↦x+y, (x,y)↦xy sur A sont modérées
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for crediting the origins of o-minimality and tame geometry, and for comparison with later locally o-minimal and ind-definable frameworks. Mathematically it is routine by today's standards.

deep.surprise_reason: The page has historical value: it shows Grothendieck's tame topology was explicitly heading toward definable expansions of fields with a bounded/ind-definable twist. The mathematics itself (definable functions form a ring, dcl(∅) is a field) is elementary and well known in o-minimality.

The phrase 'Cette condition' is struck and replaced by '(les parties a) b))', so the sentence reads '[les parties a) b)] équivalent à la validité de la [Proposition]'.
